item.title: Authorities investigating whether first Kenyan and Nigerian Ebola cases crossed paths
item.description: Nigeria this week recorded its first case of Ebola in the current outbreak, which has spread from the epicenter in Congo to several other African countries.

item.title: Military reinforcements move to Mideast. And, millions of Americans vote early
item.description: Military reinforcements are heading to the Middle East and some personnel have left the region, pointing to a potential attack on Iran. And, millions of Americans have already voted in the midterms.

item.title: Why Meta is charging to post more hyperlinks
item.description: Social media sites aren't the biggest fans of people leaving via hyperlinks. In fact, Meta has made it subscription-worthy for a Facebook Page to post more than two hyperlinks per month. What's the rationale for companies want to keep you on their site?

item.title: Israel orders closure of West Bank after soldiers kill 2 men behind an alleged attack
item.description: Israeli soldiers shot and killed two men who the military said had launched an attack near the city of Hebron in the occupied West Bank on Friday morning. At least five people were injured, including some critically.

item.title: What if you gave yourself a day to cancel all the plans you dread?
item.description: It's a day to think about all the upcoming appointments and commitments you're dreading — and then decline some of them. Writer Caroline Sylge shares a suggested schedule for the day.

item.title: With jet fuel prices near a record, holiday airfares soar higher
item.description: If you're planning to fly this holiday season, be prepared to pay more than you did last year. The price of jet fuel — one of airlines' biggest expenses — is close to an all-time high in the U.S.

item.title: Gen Z is 'in the thick' of high housing costs. These candidates aim to solve it
